title: 2009 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: When a bucket is two-thirds full of water, the bucket and water weigh \(a\) kilograms. When the bucket is one-half full of water the total weight is \(b\) kilograms. In terms of \(a\) and \(b,\) what is the total weight in kilograms when the bucket is full of water?

solutions.text:
Let \(x\) be the bucket’s weight and \(y\) the weight of a full bucket of water. Then \(x + \dfrac{2}{3}y = a\) and \(x + \dfrac{1}{2}y = b.\)

Subtracting gives \(\dfrac{1}{6}y = a - b,\) so \(y = 6a - 6b\) and \(x = b - \dfrac{1}{2}y = 4b - 3a.\) The full weight is \(x + y = 3a - 2b.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the empty bucket weigh \(x\) and a full load of water weigh \(y,\) so \(x + \tfrac{2}{3}y = a\) and \(x + \tfrac{1}{2}y = b\)
Subtract the two equations to find \(y,\) then compute \(x + y\)
